features.title: Create a project
features.summary: Creates a local project with an initial design document.
features.purpose: Give each product idea a separate workspace and revision history.
features.location: Workspace top bar, sidebar, and empty state
features.howTo: Choose New project or Create project, enter a name, and create it. Ctrl/Cmd+N also opens the form.

features.title: Open a recent project
features.summary: Lists and opens saved local projects. The workspace displays up to 12 by default; the local service supports a recent-project limit setting, but the UI has no control for it.
features.purpose: Return to active work without searching the filesystem.
features.location: Recent projects grid and workspace sidebar
features.howTo: Select a project card or a project in the Recent sidebar. Use Refresh to reload the list.

features.title: Rename a project
features.summary: Changes a project's display name while preserving its ID and contents.
features.purpose: Keep the workspace organized as a concept evolves.
features.howTo: Open a project, choose Rename, and enter the new name in the prompt.

features.title: Archive a project
features.summary: Removes a project from the active workspace list after confirmation.
features.purpose: Keep the recent workspace focused while retaining server-side archive semantics.
features.howTo: Open a project and choose Archive. Confirm the prompt.

features.title: Workspace preferences
features.summary: Stores the appearance preference and preferred AI provider in the local service.
features.purpose: Make the workspace comfortable and remember provider preference.
features.howTo: Choose System, Light, or Dark appearance; select the preferred provider; then save. Provider secrets are configured separately in AI Studio.

features.title: Command palette
features.summary: Opens shortcuts for creating projects, navigating to projects, and opening settings. The search field currently does not filter the list.
features.purpose: Make common workspace actions available from the keyboard.
features.howTo: Open Commands and choose a listed action. Ctrl/Cmd+N starts project creation; Escape closes the palette.

features.title: Manage design pages
features.summary: Adds, selects, renames, and deletes document pages; the final page cannot be deleted.
features.purpose: Keep related screens in one design document.
features.howTo: Use + to add a page, select a page to edit it, double-click or use its menu to rename, and choose Delete current page when more than one page exists.

features.title: Select and multi-select layers
features.summary: Selects a canvas layer; Ctrl/Cmd-click toggles additional layers in the selection.
features.purpose: Choose which objects to edit or arrange.
features.howTo: Click a canvas item or layer. Hold Ctrl/Cmd while clicking to add or remove an item; Escape clears selection.

features.title: Pan and zoom the canvas
features.summary: Moves the canvas viewport and changes its zoom level without changing document geometry.
features.purpose: Navigate large desktop artboards while keeping layer positions stable.
features.howTo: Choose Pan and drag the canvas, use +/− for zoom, or Ctrl/Cmd+wheel over the canvas.

features.title: Add a frame
features.summary: Adds a frame layer that can contain nested design layers.
features.purpose: Group screen content inside a bounded region.
features.howTo: Choose Frame, then select and position it on the current page.

features.title: Add text
features.summary: Adds an editable text layer to the current page.
features.purpose: Represent headings, labels, and other copy in the design.
features.howTo: Choose Text, then edit the content and typography in the Design inspector.

features.title: Add a shape
features.summary: Adds a shape layer with editable geometry and fill.
features.purpose: Build visual primitives and backgrounds.
features.howTo: Choose Shape, then adjust position, dimensions, and fill in the Design inspector.

features.title: Place a raster image
features.summary: Places a previously uploaded PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF asset on the canvas.
features.purpose: Use project imagery in a design screen.
features.howTo: Import a supported raster image in the project workspace first, then choose Image in the editor. The first available image asset is placed.

features.title: Move and resize layers
features.summary: Moves and resizes supported selected layers directly on the canvas.
features.purpose: Arrange a screen visually while editing document geometry.
features.howTo: Drag a layer to move it. Select a resizable layer and drag its resize handle to change its dimensions.

features.title: Edit layer properties
features.summary: Edits layer name, geometry, text, fill, container layout, and component-instance properties.
features.purpose: Set precise values and content for the selected layer.
features.howTo: Select a layer and update the fields shown in the Design inspector.

features.title: Toggle layer visibility
features.summary: Shows or dims a layer using the visibility control in the Layers list.
features.purpose: Temporarily hide visual content while editing.
features.howTo: Select the visibility symbol on a layer row.

features.title: Group selected layers
features.summary: Places selected sibling layers inside a container group.
features.purpose: Keep related canvas objects together.
features.howTo: Select two or more sibling layers and choose Group.

features.title: Align layers
features.summary: Moves the selected layer to the left edge or horizontal center of the current artboard.
features.purpose: Place a layer consistently on the desktop canvas.
features.howTo: Select a layer and choose Align left or Center.

features.title: Undo and redo edits
features.summary: Restores recent in-memory document states while the editor session is open.
features.purpose: Recover from recent editing actions.
features.howTo: Use the undo and redo buttons, Ctrl/Cmd+Z, and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z. Save to create a persistent revision.

features.title: Save a document revision
features.summary: Validates and saves the current document as a local project revision.
features.purpose: Persist the design and make it available to review and history.
features.howTo: Choose Save or press Ctrl/Cmd+S. The editor shows saved or unsaved status.

features.title: Choose desktop artboard size
features.summary: Switches between laptop 1280, desktop 1440, and wide desktop 1920 artboard presets.
features.purpose: Design for the product's supported desktop screen sizes.
features.howTo: Choose Laptop, Desktop, or Wide desktop from the size menu.

features.title: Lay out container children
features.summary: Arranges container children with block, flex, or grid layout and supported gap/alignment settings.
features.purpose: Create structured screen layouts.
features.location: Select a container → Design inspector → Layout
features.howTo: Select a container, choose Block, Flex, or Grid, and edit the available direction, alignment, columns, and gap fields.

features.title: Add a layout container
features.summary: Adds a parent layer whose children can use block, flex, or grid layout.
features.purpose: Group and lay out related screen content.
features.howTo: Choose Container, then set its layout in the Design inspector and place child layers within it.

features.title: Import raster images
features.summary: Stores PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF files as project assets that can be placed on a canvas.
features.purpose: Reuse local imagery in designs and exports.
features.howTo: Open a project, choose Import asset, select a supported image, then place it using the editor's Image tool.

features.title: Keep reference-only uploads
features.summary: Stores SVG and PDF uploads as downloadable references without placing them on the canvas.
features.purpose: Keep source material beside a project without implying unsupported rendering.
features.howTo: Choose Import asset and upload an SVG or PDF. Download it from the asset list; these formats are not canvas image layers.

features.title: Import Penpot v3 files
features.summary: Converts supported pages, frames, groups, text, simple shapes, color tokens, and components; keeps the source file and reports unsupported content.
features.purpose: Reuse part of a Penpot design in an editable UDS document.
features.howTo: Upload a Penpot v3 .penpot archive and review the conversion report and resulting pages.

features.title: Keep Figma .fig references
features.summary: Stores a .fig file as a downloadable reference; direct .fig decoding is not implemented.
features.purpose: Keep original source material with the project while being clear about conversion limits.
features.howTo: Upload a .fig file and download it later from the project asset list. Use the separate Figma REST file import for supported editable conversion.

features.title: Create typed design tokens
features.summary: Stores color, number, dimension, font family/size, line height, radius, shadow, and border tokens.
features.purpose: Reuse validated design values across a document.
features.howTo: Open Design system, enter a token name, choose its type and value, then add it.

features.title: Link token aliases
features.summary: Links a token to another token of the same type and resolves the alias when rendering or exporting.
features.purpose: Keep repeated values consistent and easier to update.
features.location: Design system → Add token → Alias of; token row → alias selector
features.howTo: Choose a same-type token in Alias of while creating or editing a token.

features.title: Create themes and modes
features.summary: Creates named themes and token modes with per-mode token values.
features.purpose: Represent supported visual variations within one document.
features.location: Design system → Theme and Mode controls
features.howTo: Use + Theme or + Mode, then choose the active theme and mode before editing token values.

features.title: Apply color tokens to canvas layers
features.summary: Links color tokens to selected text and shape fills so the canvas resolves the active mode value.
features.purpose: Connect reusable color decisions with actual design content.
features.howTo: Select a text or shape layer, open Design system, and choose Apply beside a color token.

features.title: Create components and variants
features.summary: Turns a supported selection into a reusable component with editable properties and variants.
features.purpose: Reuse a design element consistently across the document.
features.location: Editor toolbar → Create component; Design system → Components
features.howTo: Select a supported layer and choose Create component. Edit its definition, properties, and variants in Design system; add component instances from the component list.

features.title: Import and export UDS design systems
features.summary: Imports and exports the native UDS design-system JSON, including components.
features.purpose: Back up and reuse a complete UDS design system.
features.howTo: Choose Export UDS to download the system or Import JSON to load a supported design-system file.

features.title: Exchange DTCG, Penpot, and Tokens Studio tokens
features.summary: Exports supported DTCG tokens and imports DTCG, Penpot, and Tokens Studio JSON while reporting omitted or transformed values.
features.purpose: Move supported design tokens between compatible tools.
features.howTo: Choose Export DTCG or Import JSON, then review the transfer report for conversion notes.

features.title: Import Figma files and variables
features.summary: Reads supported Figma REST file content and variables and creates new Figma variables; direct sync requires eligible credentials and only creates new content.
features.purpose: Reuse supported Figma content and publish a UDS token set to a Figma file.
features.location: Design system → Figma file and Variables
features.howTo: Provide a Figma file key and access token with the required scopes. Import a file or variables; review the create payload and confirm before sending variables to Figma.

features.title: Connect an AI provider
features.summary: Selects a supported provider and stores its API key in the configured local credential store, such as Windows Credential Manager.
features.purpose: Enable provider-backed planning and design proposals without putting secrets in project documents.
features.howTo: Choose a supported provider and enter its API key when prompted. Verify the connected status before using provider-backed actions.

features.title: Draft a user flow and screen inventory
features.summary: Uses a product brief to propose a user flow and editable screen inventory, which can be reviewed before screen generation.
features.purpose: Translate product intent into a structured starting plan.
features.howTo: Connect an AI provider, describe the users/problem/outcome, choose screen and direction counts, then draft and review the plan.

features.title: Generate editable design directions
features.summary: Generates structured proposals and can apply a selected direction as editable pages after review.
features.purpose: Explore visual directions from an approved screen plan.
features.howTo: After reviewing the flow and screen inventory, choose Generate directions, review the proposal and quality notes, then apply a direction.

features.title: Review AI revision proposals
features.summary: Drafts scoped changes for selected layers and lets users accept selected operations before applying.
features.purpose: Use AI to refine specific selected content while retaining user review and revision checks.
features.howTo: Select layers, enter the requested change, draft a proposal, choose operations, and apply the accepted changes. Save to persist them.

features.title: Run a local design quality review
features.summary: Checks the current document and generated proposals with local structural and quality checks.
features.purpose: Expose issues for review before exporting or continuing a design.
features.howTo: Open Quality review and inspect the checks; refresh the review after changing the document.

features.title: Add selected reference images to an AI request
features.summary: Allows up to three supported project images to be selected for provider-backed context.
features.purpose: Provide visual references for an AI design task.
features.location: AI Studio → Plan & generate → Reference screenshots or images
features.howTo: Import raster images into the project first, then select up to three images in AI Studio before sending a request.

features.title: Define prototype variables
features.summary: Creates text, number, and boolean values scoped to the prototype.
features.purpose: Represent state that can change during a click-through demo.
features.howTo: Enter a name, choose the type and initial value, and choose Add variable.

features.title: Bind variables to text
features.summary: Connects a prototype variable to a selected text layer.
features.purpose: Show changing values in a prototype preview.
features.location: Prototype & UX → Bind a variable to text
features.howTo: Select a text layer in the canvas, choose a variable, and choose Bind.

features.title: Configure prototype interactions
features.summary: Connects a selected layer to navigation, overlays, variable updates, or component variant changes using click, double-click, or hover triggers.
features.purpose: Demonstrate a user flow without changing the design document during preview.
features.howTo: Select a source layer, choose the trigger/action and its target or value, then add the interaction.

features.title: Preview a clickable prototype
features.summary: Runs configured interactions inside a sandboxed iframe; preview changes do not modify the design document.
features.purpose: Review navigation and interactive behavior safely.
features.howTo: Add pages and interactions, then choose Open clickable preview.

features.title: Check prototype UX and accessibility
features.summary: Reports reachability, entry points, trigger keyboard support, source visibility, image descriptions, and variable bindings.
features.purpose: Catch structural and accessibility issues before sharing a prototype preview.
features.howTo: Open the panel and review each check; fix issues in the canvas or interaction settings.

features.title: Comment on a page or layer
features.summary: Creates a saved comment thread anchored to a project/document revision, page, and optional layer.
features.purpose: Record review feedback alongside the saved design state.
features.howTo: Save the document, optionally select a layer, enter feedback in New comment, and choose Add comment.

features.title: Reply to and manage comment threads
features.summary: Supports replies and open/resolved/all filtering, with resolve and reopen actions.
features.purpose: Track local feedback through resolution.
features.howTo: Reply to an open thread, resolve it when addressed, and change the filter to view resolved or all threads.

features.title: Compare saved revisions
features.summary: Compares two saved revisions and summarizes page/layer changes plus design-system and prototype change flags.
features.purpose: Understand what changed between saved document states.
features.location: Editor → History or Review → Revision compare
features.howTo: Save at least two revisions, choose From and To revisions, and select Compare.

features.title: Restore a prior revision
features.summary: Restores an earlier saved state as a new immutable revision while preserving existing history.
features.purpose: Return to an earlier design without erasing the revision trail.
features.howTo: Compare revisions, choose a previous revision in the comparison, and select Restore as a new revision.

features.title: Download a code bundle
features.summary: Exports the supported design as a React/Vite project, static HTML/CSS, tokens, referenced images, and setup notes.
features.purpose: Give developers a portable starting point for implementation.
features.howTo: Review included files and export notes, then choose Download code bundle.

features.title: Review export diagnostics
features.summary: Reports unsupported or lossy constructs before code export.
features.purpose: Show what the generated output can preserve and what needs follow-up.
features.howTo: Open Code handoff and read the Export notes before downloading the bundle.

features.title: Preview restricted static output
features.summary: Displays generated static HTML in an iframe with scripts, network, forms, and external images blocked.
features.purpose: Inspect exported appearance without running generated code.
features.howTo: Choose Open restricted preview. The preview is intentionally static and isolated.

features.title: Prepare a Git-ready export
features.summary: Adds a .gitignore and local setup instructions to the downloaded bundle; it does not initialize Git or push to GitHub.
features.purpose: Make a downloaded bundle easier to adopt in a local repository.
features.location: Code handoff → Prepare for local Git
features.howTo: Select Prepare for local Git before downloading the bundle.

features.title: MCP: list projects
features.summary: Returns bounded metadata for local projects to a connected MCP host.
features.purpose: Let an authorized desktop agent discover available UDS projects.
features.location: External MCP client connected to the local UDS server
features.howTo: Start the local MCP server and call list_projects from an enabled MCP client.

features.title: MCP: read project summary
features.summary: Returns bounded project counts and revision metadata without returning full document snapshots.
features.purpose: Give an agent a compact view of a project's saved structure.
features.howTo: Call get_project_summary with a project ID from list_projects.

features.title: MCP: read selected node summaries
features.summary: Returns up to 50 summaries for explicitly requested nodes, with text truncated to 500 characters.
features.purpose: Let an agent inspect a narrow, user-chosen part of a saved design.
features.howTo: Provide a project ID, page ID, and the node IDs to summarize.

features.title: MCP: revision-checked text and rename writes
features.summary: The server implements set_layer_text and rename_layer commands that require an expected revision; the current Antigravity connection does not expose them.
features.purpose: Offer narrowly scoped edits while preserving document revision checks.
features.location: External MCP client; write tools are not enabled in the current Antigravity connection
features.howTo: An MCP host must explicitly enable the write tools and review each proposed mutation before use.

externalDependencies.title: A configured AI provider
externalDependencies.reason: Provider-backed requests require a valid key and configured provider. Live provider behavior is not verified without user credentials.

externalDependencies.title: Eligible Figma account and file scopes
externalDependencies.reason: File and Variables REST endpoints require the appropriate account, file permissions, and API scopes.

externalDependencies.title: Local MCP server and compatible host
externalDependencies.reason: MCP tools are available only when the user starts the local server and connects an external MCP client.

unavailableUi.title: Account menu
unavailableUi.reason: The avatar is a visual placeholder; there is no sign-in, account profile, or identity flow.

unavailableUi.title: Custom AI provider adapter
unavailableUi.reason: The option is visible but disabled; only the listed built-in providers can be configured.

importantDependencies: Canvas image placement depends on importing a PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF project asset first.
AI planning, generation, and revision proposals require a configured provider key; design quality review runs locally.
Layer comments require a saved revision and are local-only; they do not create user identities or cloud sharing.
Revision comparison requires at least two saved revisions; restoration creates a new revision.
Figma file/variable features require valid file access and the relevant API scopes; some content is omitted with a report.
MCP tools require the local MCP server and an external compatible host; optional write tools are not enabled in the current Antigravity connection.
